newsitem.title: DENMARK: East and West meet on Baltic security.
newsitem.headline: East and West meet on Baltic security.

text.p: Defence ministers from the United States and eight European countries converged on Copenhagen on Monday for talks on security in the Baltic region amid an uncharacteristic Danish government press blackout.

United States Defence Secretary William Perry arrived on a U.S. military aircraft and was whisked away without meeting journalists. "The Danish defence ministry has asked everyone not to make any statements to the media," a diplomat said.
Talks will focus on ways of integrating the three Baltic states of Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia into Western defence structures while not being part of the U.S.-led NATO alliance.

Taking part in the seminar, which will continue on Tuesday, will be Perry, Denmark's Hans Haekkerup, British Defence Secretary Michael Portillo, Germany's Volker Ruehe and their counterparts from Sweden, the Netherlands and the three Baltic states.
Russia will be represented by a Russia-North America think-tank while Poland and Norway are sending senior defence officals.
No decisions will be taken in Copenhagen.

But views could emerge that Perry and NATO defence ministers will be able to pass on to their Russian counterpart Igor Rodionov when they meet him at a separate conference in Norway on Wednesday and Thursday.

Sources close to the talks expect them to discuss tying the three Baltic republics -- all former Soviet republics -- into NATO's Baltic regional command in Denmark. They will also discuss the future role of a Baltic peacekeeping battalion.
The talks may also look at ways of easing mutual distrust between Russia and the three Baltic states.

"It will take place in a relaxed and informal atmosphere ...participants will be able to think aloud. There will be no hard and fast conclusions and the press will be kept far away from the closed doors," the Danish daily Berlingske Tidende summed up on Monday.
